Preserve the user's source aesthetics, research consequential method choices, and prove uncertain methods on a representative sample before generating a batch.

Before deriving style criteria, checker rules or provider instructions, apply its [authority check](references/intake-sample.md#keep-authority-through-derived-rules). Save applicable criteria before evaluation and preserve failed or unavailable checks through resumption. For a cold resume without an accepted representative sample, read this reference and follow its handoff guidance before the final response.
23	
24	Keep requirement authority through each translation: explicit user/project constraints, observations and proposals remain distinct in the provider request and review criteria. Read [the artistic-authority checks](references/artistic-authority.md) when deriving aesthetic restrictions or auditing a contradictory approach; the retained examples are conditional guidance.
25	
26	Use the [candidate inspection operation](references/inspection.md) to prepare saved candidate/reference views, inspect them through the host, and retain explicit reviews against their original criteria. Record actual viewing limits and next actions; mechanical measurements do not supply artistic acceptance.
27	
28	Use the [provider submission and recovery operation](references/provider-recovery.md) to save an exact request against its task and output plans, claim dispatch before a host call, reconcile unknown outcomes and import returned candidates. Read both workflow and job status before starting another request.
29	
30	Use the [family and delivery operation](references/family-delivery.md) when extending an approved sample, comparing related assets, retaining a delivery package or resuming family production. Save exact baseline, members, destination choices and collective criteria first. Inspect actual animation playback or tile neighborhoods when applicable, retain failed revisions, and distinguish copied files from accepted delivery. Start cold sessions with family, workflow and job reports.
31	
32	The compiled operational knowledge is [library.px](../../resources/knowledge/library.px). Retrieve one method with `context <resolved library.px> k.<method-id> --root <resolved resources directory>`. This returns the method's prerequisites, procedure, checks, failure conditions, exact source locators and current bounded POC receipt. Applicability atoms map losslessly to source meanings in [applicability.json](../../resources/knowledge/applicability.json). Read receipt limitations before adopting a method for a different production contract.
33	
34	The bundled runner is `../../scripts/pixl.py`; the runtime is `../../runtime/`. Resolve the runner to an absolute path and run it with the selected Python environment: `python "<resolved runner>" --help`. It requires Python 3.11+, Pillow 10+, and jsonschema 4.18+; install the bundled `../../requirements.txt` into the selected environment. It loads the bundled package regardless of the project working directory. Keep mutable state and outputs in the user's project. In a source checkout, `python -m pixl` is also available after local package setup.
35	
36	Before a remote action, discover the actual PixelLab tools and their schemas in the harness. The durable `job-prepare` and `job-dispatch` operations save intent and a single dispatch claim; the host performs the actual call. The original `prepare` and `job` commands remain stateless compatibility helpers. The local PIXL state server does not submit or poll PixelLab. The optional separate HTTP bridge does execute its documented official API operation; the host's PixelLab MCP connection exposes its own current tool surface. Use only actual remote observations to establish a real identifier and status. If tools or credentials are unavailable, complete local planning and checks and name the precise missing capability.
37	
38	Validate mechanical constraints, inspect images visually, and verify required engine import behavior before accepting an asset. Report what was checked and what remains uncertain. Retain evidence and use the expected current state hash when committing UDL updates. `pixl_commit` accepts a JSON `document` directly or a `candidate` wire-file path; both use the same validation. Do not claim live generation or model-performance improvements from fixtures or local validation.

1	# Provider submission and recovery operation
2	
3	Use this operation when a PIXL production task needs an external generation request, a submitted attempt needs resumption, or a returned candidate needs to enter project state. Developing this operation is a maintainer task; only a production assignment or explicit evaluation activates PIXL.
4	
5	Read the [PX2 specification](../../../resources/spec/PIXL-2.md), its [registry](../../../runtime/pixl/registry-v2.json), and the [journal contract](../../../resources/spec/provider-recovery.md). This operation uses the explicit J.jr/op/xs extension. Existing unjournaled J and PX1 stores keep their earlier meanings; adding fields or changing a header does not manufacture durable history.
6	
7	## Required context
8	
9	- The project root, current store state/hash, task and selected planned F outputs. Use the [intake/sample operation](intake-sample.md) first if choices or criteria are missing. Sample tasks may test proposals; dependent production still needs adoption and confirmation.
10	- The actual connected provider identity, selected tool and exact inputSchema observed through this harness, with a retained discovery source, timestamp and evidence. A cached capabilities list is advisory. If live tools are absent, preserve the plan and explain the missing capability; do not invent a discovery observation.
11	- The user's established authorized scope and budget, retained as a scope string and evidence object. Existing authorization can support this record; a local tool does not grant new authority. Resolve a consequential missing budget/permission before a paid call while continuing independent work.
12	- For recovery, the saved intent and every retained observation. For import, the actual already downloaded file and evidence relating it to this returned resource. Keep credentials out of arguments, schema examples, discovery, authorization and response evidence.
13	
14	Resolve `../../../scripts/pixl.py` relative to this reference directory and invoke its absolute path using the selected Python environment. The commands below omit that common prefix. Use the same project `--root ROOT` throughout; STORE is a subdirectory of ROOT. Every mutation consumes the current `--expect HASH` and returns the next hash. Files and evidence belong in the project, outside installed resources.
15	
16	## Prepare a saved request
17	
18	Prefer the actual connected official PixelLab MCP operation when it fits the task. Use [operation and reference selection](pixellab-operations.md) first: confirm the native canvas, reference roles and output packaging. Preserve image transport identifiers with their local source hashes. The optional HTTP route below is a selected integration, not a substitute for every MCP workflow.
19	
20	When the host exposes the optional PixelLab HTTP bridge, use `pixellab_contract`
21	to inspect its retained official HTTP schema, source date and simulated/live flag.
22	It currently supports one async image operation. This is a dated HTTP contract,
23	not live MCP discovery; HTTP `image_size` is distinct from MCP width/height aliases.
24	`pixellab_prepare_image` validates and saves the request against the planned task
25	and output. Then `pixellab_submit` claims, submits once and records the response;
26	do not call local `job-dispatch` first. `pixellab_poll` observes the saved ID once
27	(allow the returned interval between real polls), and `pixellab_import_image`
28	decodes and retains a completed response as an unaccepted candidate. Each mutation
29	requires the current store hash. Continue with normal inspection and acceptance.
30	Unknown submission outcomes cannot be resubmitted; preserve and reconcile them.
31	Mocked bridge observations remain simulated, including in handoffs.
32	
33	1. Run `workflow STORE/state.px --root ROOT` and `jobs STORE/state.px --root ROOT`. Read both lifecycle blockers and existing provider attempts. An open task does not imply permission to create another remote job. Pending prepared/unknown/submitted/running work on the output must be resolved first.
34	2. Retrieve the task's focused context. Translate its intended output and relevant inputs, decisions, methods and contract into the actual tool schema. Preserve arguments exactly; describe any requirement the tool cannot express and the later acceptance check that will evaluate it.
35	3. Write a request JSON object with exactly `provider`, `tool`, `arguments`, `schema`, `discovery`, and `authorization`. `schema` is the full inputSchema object. Discovery has `source`, `observed_at`, `evidence`; authorization has `scope`, `evidence`. Evidence must be nonempty objects. Timestamps require an explicit UTC offset and at most six fractional digits. Capture observation time from the host clock when observing/recording the response (for example, Python datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()); keep provider event time separate. Do not invent a precise time from the session date, and omit optional timestamps that were not observed. Values come from the current assignment and observations, not from a bundled art fixture.
36	4. Run `job-prepare STORE JOB TASK REQUEST_JSON --outputs OUTPUT ... --expect HASH --root ROOT`. This saves exact request/schema/provenance/authorization and the relevant plan hashes. Read its cached assessment: a conflict is a reason to inspect current documentation and tool semantics, not to silently rewrite the request or substitute the cache for the observed schema. Schema validity alone cannot establish account entitlement, output quality or actual cost.
37	
38	Preparation is complete when state contains the prepared J and immutable journal X/E. No remote action has occurred. A missing tool, unresolved project requirement or missing authorization leaves useful local planning intact.
39	
40	## Claim once, then call the actual provider
41	
42	Run `job-dispatch STORE JOB --expect HASH --root ROOT`. Only a successful publication returns `dispatch_request`. It first records a local dispatch claim and moves the saved job to **unknown**, before the host sends anything. Use exactly the returned provider/tool/arguments for the one authorized host call. 43	
44	The local command does not submit, poll, authenticate or download. `remote_executed: false` describes the local tool even when its journal later records a caller-observed success. Real provider effects remain the host's responsibility.
45	
46	Retain the response without credentials and use `job-observe STORE JOB STATE EVIDENCE_JSON --remote-id RETURNED_ID --expect HASH --root ROOT`. After identity is known, omitting `--remote-id` preserves it; it cannot be rebound. Repeat running/unknown observations only when supported by actual observations. A failed or succeeded outcome is terminal for observations.
47	
48	If submission returns no usable answer, record `unknown` with the actual timeout/transport evidence when available. Never treat the initial unknown claim as evidence that a provider received the request, and never treat a missing ID as evidence that it did not.
49	
50	For delegated work, compare the saved prepared request with the exact arguments in the [reviewed request packet](request-review.md) before dispatch. Changed arguments or criteria require an updated comparison; an unchanged reviewed contract does not require the user to repeat authorization.
51	
52	## Resume and reconcile
53	
54	Start with `jobs STORE/state.px --root ROOT`. It returns the saved request, context, event history, remote identity, candidate associations, drift and next action. Reading a request is not a new dispatch grant.
55	
56	A resource ID belongs to the connection that returned it. Use that same provider/account context for lookup or retrieval; never carry a simulated or unrelated provider ID into a real service. If the originating connection cannot return an image, retain that limitation and its observed state. Separate future production uses its own actual request and provider identity under the assignment; it is not retrieval of the simulated job. A finished request-only assignment does not terminate its queued job: before another request for the same asset, resolve the pending attempt with supported originating-connection evidence, or keep a truly separate assignment/context explicit. 58	| Saved state / issue | Next operation |
59	|---|---|
60	| Prepared, context current, no blockers | Claim with job-dispatch before one host call |
61	| Prepared, plan drift or lifecycle blocker | Resolve the specific context; abandon obsolete intent with an evidenced failed observation if appropriate, then prepare a new request ID |
62	| Unknown | Reconcile using the actual provider's documented lookup/status capabilities and retained evidence; do not dispatch or recreate |
63	| Submitted/running with ID | Inspect that exact resource using its discovered status tool, then record the observed response |
64	| Succeeded | Retrieve the actual output through the host, import local candidate bytes, then evaluate acceptance |
65	| Failed | Preserve failure, establish its consequence and any still-valid retry authorization, then use a new job ID for a new attempt |
66	| Legacy unjournaled job | Inspect its actual available history manually; do not attach a fictional journal or ignore pending work |
67	| File/hash error | Preserve the diagnostic and restore the exact retained bytes from available history/backups before continuing; do not rewrite receipts to make a changed file pass |
68	
69	A crash between claim and host submission also leaves unknown. If no provider lookup can resolve whether the request was sent, leave that uncertainty explicit and continue independent work. Elapsed time cannot authorize a retry. A confirmed non-acceptance or terminal failure may support a failed observation and a newly authorized attempt; record that evidence first. Automatic remote exactly-once delivery is not claimed.
70	
71	On `stale_write` or `store_locked`, no dispatch grant was returned. Reread the state and owner information, then reconcile the attempted local change. Do not blindly repeat job-dispatch if another writer already claimed it. Immutable blobs left by a failed publication are unreferenced preparation data; state.px is the publication authority.
72	
73	## Import and hand back to acceptance
74	
75	Download with the actual host/provider mechanism into the project. Then run `job-import STORE JOB OUTPUT CANDIDATE DOWNLOADED_PATH EVIDENCE_JSON --expect HASH --root ROOT`. DOWNLOADED_PATH is relative to ROOT. This copies a byte snapshot into the store and creates X.of for the original F, plus a retained import event and J.xs reference. It preserves the downloaded original. It does not nominate the candidate, measure the image, grant V, or finish T.
76

A new interpretation must not relabel an old generation as though it used the new contract. Submitted observations can still be recorded while the plan has drifted.

# Provider submission and recovery operation

Use this operation when a PIXL production task needs an external generation request, a submitted attempt needs resumption, or a returned candidate needs to enter project state. Developing this operation is a maintainer task; only a production assignment or explicit evaluation activates PIXL.

Read the [PX2 specification](../../../resources/spec/PIXL-2.md), its [registry](../../../runtime/pixl/registry-v2.json), and the [journal contract](../../../resources/spec/provider-recovery.md). This operation uses the explicit J.jr/op/xs extension. Existing unjournaled J and PX1 stores keep their earlier meanings; adding fields or changing a header does not manufacture durable history.

## Required context

- The project root, current store state/hash, task and selected planned F outputs. Use the [intake/sample operation](intake-sample.md) first if choices or criteria are missing. Sample tasks may test proposals; dependent production still needs adoption and confirmation.
- The actual connected provider identity, selected tool and exact inputSchema observed through this harness, with a retained discovery source, timestamp and evidence. A cached capabilities list is advisory. If live tools are absent, preserve the plan and explain the missing capability; do not invent a discovery observation.
- The user's established authorized scope and budget, retained as a scope string and evidence object. Existing authorization can support this record; a local tool does not grant new authority. Resolve a consequential missing budget/permission before a paid call while continuing independent work.
- For recovery, the saved intent and every retained observation. For import, the actual already downloaded file and evidence relating it to this returned resource. Keep credentials out of arguments, schema examples, discovery, authorization and response evidence.

Resolve `../../../scripts/pixl.py` relative to this reference directory and invoke its absolute path using the selected Python environment. The commands below omit that common prefix. Use the same project `--root ROOT` throughout; STORE is a subdirectory of ROOT. Every mutation consumes the current `--expect HASH` and returns the next hash. Files and evidence belong in the project, outside installed resources.

## Prepare a saved request

Prefer the actual connected official PixelLab MCP operation when it fits the task. Use [operation and reference selection](pixellab-operations.md) first: confirm the native canvas, reference roles and output packaging. Preserve image transport identifiers with their local source hashes. The optional HTTP route below is a selected integration, not a substitute for every MCP workflow.

When the host exposes the optional PixelLab HTTP bridge, use `pixellab_contract`
to inspect its retained official HTTP schema, source date and simulated/live flag.
It currently supports one async image operation. This is a dated HTTP contract,
not live MCP discovery; HTTP `image_size` is distinct from MCP width/height aliases.
`pixellab_prepare_image` validates and saves the request against the planned task
and output. Then `pixellab_submit` claims, submits once and records the response;
do not call local `job-dispatch` first. `pixellab_poll` observes the saved ID once
(allow the returned interval between real polls), and `pixellab_import_image`
decodes and retains a completed response as an unaccepted candidate. Each mutation
requires the current store hash. Continue with normal inspection and acceptance.
Unknown submission outcomes cannot be resubmitted; preserve and reconcile them.
Mocked bridge observations remain simulated, including in handoffs.

1. Run `workflow STORE/state.px --root ROOT` and `jobs STORE/state.px --root ROOT`. Read both lifecycle blockers and existing provider attempts. An open task does not imply permission to create another remote job. Pending prepared/unknown/submitted/running work on the output must be resolved first.
2. Retrieve the task's focused context. Translate its intended output and relevant inputs, decisions, methods and contract into the actual tool schema. Preserve arguments exactly; describe any requirement the tool cannot express and the later acceptance check that will evaluate it.
3. Write a request JSON object with exactly `provider`, `tool`, `arguments`, `schema`, `discovery`, and `authorization`. `schema` is the full inputSchema object. Discovery has `source`, `observed_at`, `evidence`; authorization has `scope`, `evidence`. Evidence must be nonempty objects. Timestamps require an explicit UTC offset and at most six fractional digits. Capture observation time from the host clock when observing/recording the response (for example, Python datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()); keep provider event time separate. Do not invent a precise time from the session date, and omit optional timestamps that were not observed. Values come from the current assignment and observations, not from a bundled art fixture.
4. Run `job-prepare STORE JOB TASK REQUEST_JSON --outputs OUTPUT ... --expect HASH --root ROOT`. This saves exact request/schema/provenance/authorization and the relevant plan hashes. Read its cached assessment: a conflict is a reason to inspect current documentation and tool semantics, not to silently rewrite the request or substitute the cache for the observed schema. Schema validity alone cannot establish account entitlement, output quality or actual cost.

Preparation is complete when state contains the prepared J and immutable journal X/E. No remote action has occurred. A missing tool, unresolved project requirement or missing authorization leaves useful local planning intact.

## Claim once, then call the actual provider

Run `job-dispatch STORE JOB --expect HASH --root ROOT`. Only a successful publication returns `dispatch_request`. It first records a local dispatch claim and moves the saved job to **unknown**, before the host sends anything. Use exactly the returned provider/tool/arguments for the one authorized host call. Do not add defaults or replace arguments after claiming; that would be a different request.

The local command does not submit, poll, authenticate or download. `remote_executed: false` describes the local tool even when its journal later records a caller-observed success. Real provider effects remain the host's responsibility.

Retain the response without credentials and use `job-observe STORE JOB STATE EVIDENCE_JSON --remote-id RETURNED_ID --expect HASH --root ROOT`. Accepted states submitted/running/succeeded require the actual observed identifier. A supplied failure can be recorded without inventing an ID. After identity is known, omitting `--remote-id` preserves it; it cannot be rebound. Repeat running/unknown observations only when supported by actual observations. A failed or succeeded outcome is terminal for observations.

If submission returns no usable answer, record `unknown` with the actual timeout/transport evidence when available. Never treat the initial unknown claim as evidence that a provider received the request, and never treat a missing ID as evidence that it did not.

For delegated work, compare the saved prepared request with the exact arguments in the [reviewed request packet](request-review.md) before dispatch. Changed arguments or criteria require an updated comparison; an unchanged reviewed contract does not require the user to repeat authorization.

## Resume and reconcile

Start with `jobs STORE/state.px --root ROOT`. It returns the saved request, context, event history, remote identity, candidate associations, drift and next action. Reading a request is not a new dispatch grant.

A resource ID belongs to the connection that returned it. Use that same provider/account context for lookup or retrieval; never carry a simulated or unrelated provider ID into a real service. If the originating connection cannot return an image, retain that limitation and its observed state. Separate future production uses its own actual request and provider identity under the assignment; it is not retrieval of the simulated job. A finished request-only assignment does not terminate its queued job: before another request for the same asset, resolve the pending attempt with supported originating-connection evidence, or keep a truly separate assignment/context explicit. Changing task/output IDs within the asset store cannot bypass its pending attempt.

| Saved state / issue | Next operation |
|---|---|
| Prepared, context current, no blockers | Claim with job-dispatch before one host call |
| Prepared, plan drift or lifecycle blocker | Resolve the specific context; abandon obsolete intent with an evidenced failed observation if appropriate, then prepare a new request ID |
| Unknown | Reconcile using the actual provider's documented lookup/status capabilities and retained evidence; do not dispatch or recreate |
| Submitted/running with ID | Inspect that exact resource using its discovered status tool, then record the observed response |
| Succeeded | Retrieve the actual output through the host, import local candidate bytes, then evaluate acceptance |
| Failed | Preserve failure, establish its consequence and any still-valid retry authorization, then use a new job ID for a new attempt |
| Legacy unjournaled job | Inspect its actual available history manually; do not attach a fictional journal or ignore pending work |

Elapsed time cannot authorize a retry. A confirmed non-acceptance or terminal failure may support a failed observation and a newly authorized attempt; record that evidence first. Automatic remote exactly-once delivery is not claimed.

On `stale_write` or `store_locked`, no dispatch grant was returned. Reread the state and owner information, then reconcile the attempted local change. ## Import and hand back to acceptance

Download with the actual host/provider mechanism into the project. Then run `job-import STORE JOB OUTPUT CANDIDATE DOWNLOADED_PATH EVIDENCE_JSON --expect HASH --root ROOT`. DOWNLOADED_PATH is relative to ROOT. This copies a byte snapshot into the store and creates X.of for the original F, plus a retained import event and J.xs reference. It preserves the downloaded original. It does not nominate the candidate, measure the image, grant V, or finish T.

Import rejects changed output/contract/criterion context. Keep the returned file and original history; reconcile the intended plan explicitly before associating it. A new interpretation must not relabel an old generation as though it used the new contract. Submitted observations can still be recorded while the plan has drifted.

Retrieve the imported X to obtain its retained path/hash. Run relevant mechanical inspection, review the actual image at native and enlarged scale, and exercise the required destination checks. Follow the [intake/sample acceptance procedure](intake-sample.md) to nominate a candidate deliberately and record each Q's pass, fail or unavailable verdict. Provider success and journal-retention receipts cannot satisfy those requirements.

1	# Production procedure
2	
3	Read this when creating, reviewing, or integrating assets. The [profile](../../../resources/agent/PROFILE.md) defines the full contract.
4	
5	For incomplete intake, sample planning, criterion verdicts, revision and cold resumption, use the concrete [PX2 intake/sample operation](intake-sample.md). It defines the saved-state steps that support this production procedure. Keep existing PX1 projects in their declared version.
6	
7	For an approved sample, multiple related members, collective continuity or delivery, use the [family and delivery operation](family-delivery.md). It defines saved baseline/member/destination plans, comparison in playback or neighborhoods, rejected revisions, retained copied files, and the exact unfinished destination checks a cold session must resume. A family snapshot creates a candidate; its acceptance remains a separate review.
8	
9	## Intake to a useful proof
10	
11	Inspect the user-provided references and existing assets, including their actual dimensions. State the asset's gameplay role and destination. Resolve only decisions that affect this task: native canvas size, projection, silhouette, color/ramp policy, edge treatment, lighting, transparency, directions, frame timing, anchors, tile boundaries, and renderer/import rules. Do not make a generic checklist into a mandatory style.
12	
13	For each consequential choice retain WHO owns the constraint or result, WHAT will change, WHERE it is applied, and WHY the source or evidence supports it. A choice can come from the user, existing project material, observed visual references, documented tool limitations, or an explicitly identified proposal. Every recorded UDL decision must include research references and applicable executed proof receipts as defined by the specification. Researched knowledge can remain without executed proof until adoption. When sources conflict, identify the conflict and resolve it before dependent execution.
14	
15	For unfamiliar methods or uncertain output quality, define a focused proof of concept:
16	
17	| Field | Required meaning |
18	| --- | --- |
19	| Question | One uncertainty that affects the planned asset family |
20	| Method | The researched tool or technique and source that supports it |
21	| Smallest artifact | A representative pose, cycle, seam neighborhood, rig assembly, or import fixture |
22	| Acceptance | An observable test stated before interpreting results |
23	| Result | Artifact path/hash, measurements, visual observations, and pass/fail/uncertain |
24	| Consequence | Proceed, revise, or stop the dependent batch and why |
25	
26	Examples: prove diagonal tile joins with a repeated neighborhood; prove a walk cycle's grounded contact and pivot stability before producing all directions; prove material-color response and occlusion separately before promising dynamic sprite lighting. A proof must exercise the disputed behavior. A prose plan alone is not a proof of concept.
27	
28	## Remote operation
29	
30	Use [PixelLab operation selection](pixellab-operations.md) to match the deliverable and each reference role to supported arguments. Carry actual image data/handles, not merely file names in text. Use [the delegation contract](delegation.md) for work received from and returned to another agent.
31	
32	Read the tool schemas actually available in the session and the relevant current [PixelLab MCP documentation](https://api.pixellab.ai/mcp/docs). Record which surface is being used and the evidence date; cached examples do not establish current availability. Check prerequisites and map the selected UDL contract to supported tool arguments. Preserve references and values that the selected tool can express; report any constraint requiring later editing or inspection.
33	
34	Follow the [provider submission and recovery operation](provider-recovery.md) for new PX2 work: save the exact request and plan, claim dispatch locally before one actual PixelLab call, retain returned identifiers and observations, and reconcile unknown outcomes before any new attempt. Import downloaded bytes as candidates, then evaluate them separately. Existing authorization and budget govern real calls. Do not synthesize progress or convert elapsed time into a completed state.
35	
36	## Artifact acceptance
37	
38	Retrieve the actual artifact before evaluating it. Record provenance, returned identifiers, local path, content hash, and contract version. Use `asset-check` for the dimensions and any palette constraint the project actually requires. Supplement it with appropriate format/frame/alpha checks; check `--help` and the current runtime output to establish its exact coverage.
39	
40	Inspect native-scale readability and enlarged clusters. Evaluate identity and style across the asset family. Inspect animation in playback as well as individual frames, and tiles in repeated neighborhoods. Mechanical checks cannot measure all these properties. # Production procedure

Read this when creating, reviewing, or integrating assets. The [profile](../../../resources/agent/PROFILE.md) defines the full contract.

For incomplete intake, sample planning, criterion verdicts, revision and cold resumption, use the concrete [PX2 intake/sample operation](intake-sample.md). It defines the saved-state steps that support this production procedure. Keep existing PX1 projects in their declared version.

For an approved sample, multiple related members, collective continuity or delivery, use the [family and delivery operation](family-delivery.md). It defines saved baseline/member/destination plans, comparison in playback or neighborhoods, rejected revisions, retained copied files, and the exact unfinished destination checks a cold session must resume. A family snapshot creates a candidate; its acceptance remains a separate review.

## Intake to a useful proof

Inspect the user-provided references and existing assets, including their actual dimensions. State the asset's gameplay role and destination. Resolve only decisions that affect this task: native canvas size, projection, silhouette, color/ramp policy, edge treatment, lighting, transparency, directions, frame timing, anchors, tile boundaries, and renderer/import rules. Do not make a generic checklist into a mandatory style.

For each consequential choice retain WHO owns the constraint or result, WHAT will change, WHERE it is applied, and WHY the source or evidence supports it. A choice can come from the user, existing project material, observed visual references, documented tool limitations, or an explicitly identified proposal. Every recorded UDL decision must include research references and applicable executed proof receipts as defined by the specification. Researched knowledge can remain without executed proof until adoption. When sources conflict, identify the conflict and resolve it before dependent execution.

For unfamiliar methods or uncertain output quality, define a focused proof of concept:

| Field | Required meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Question | One uncertainty that affects the planned asset family |
| Method | The researched tool or technique and source that supports it |
| Smallest artifact | A representative pose, cycle, seam neighborhood, rig assembly, or import fixture |
| Acceptance | An observable test stated before interpreting results |
| Result | Artifact path/hash, measurements, visual observations, and pass/fail/uncertain |
| Consequence | Proceed, revise, or stop the dependent batch and why |

Examples: prove diagonal tile joins with a repeated neighborhood; prove a walk cycle's grounded contact and pivot stability before producing all directions; prove material-color response and occlusion separately before promising dynamic sprite lighting. A proof must exercise the disputed behavior. A prose plan alone is not a proof of concept.

## Remote operation

Use [PixelLab operation selection](pixellab-operations.md) to match the deliverable and each reference role to supported arguments. Carry actual image data/handles, not merely file names in text. Use [the delegation contract](delegation.md) for work received from and returned to another agent.

Read the tool schemas actually available in the session and the relevant current [PixelLab MCP documentation](https://api.pixellab.ai/mcp/docs). Record which surface is being used and the evidence date; cached examples do not establish current availability. Check prerequisites and map the selected UDL contract to supported tool arguments. Preserve references and values that the selected tool can express; report any constraint requiring later editing or inspection.

Follow the [provider submission and recovery operation](provider-recovery.md) for new PX2 work: save the exact request and plan, claim dispatch locally before one actual PixelLab call, retain returned identifiers and observations, and reconcile unknown outcomes before any new attempt. Import downloaded bytes as candidates, then evaluate them separately. Existing authorization and budget govern real calls. Do not synthesize progress or convert elapsed time into a completed state.

## Artifact acceptance

Retrieve the actual artifact before evaluating it. Record provenance, returned identifiers, local path, content hash, and contract version. Use `asset-check` for the dimensions and any palette constraint the project actually requires. Supplement it with appropriate format/frame/alpha checks; check `--help` and the current runtime output to establish its exact coverage.

Inspect native-scale readability and enlarged clusters. Evaluate identity and style across the asset family. Inspect animation in playback as well as individual frames, and tiles in repeated neighborhoods. Mechanical checks cannot measure all these properties. Keep the visual verdict separate from tool measurements and do not mark an unviewed artifact visually approved.

In the destination engine, validate applicable import sampling, pixel/display scale, alpha edges, atlas padding, pivots, frame slicing, timing, direction mapping, material and lighting behavior. If the engine is unavailable, deliver the artifact with an explicit unverified import requirement. Preserve any failed trial separately from the accepted revision and explain the change that resolved it.

Finish with the useful outcome, artifact links, source/contract identity, observed job state, concise verification evidence, known limitations, and next dependency. Update production state through the runtime so a later agent can resume without repeating remote generation or losing unresolved issues.

1	# Approved sample through family delivery
2	
3	Use this operation when extending a reviewed representative sample into related assets, comparing their continuity, retaining a delivery package, or resuming an existing family. It governs PIXL production. A developer maintaining these instructions remains in the development role.
4	
5	## Start with the actual saved family
6	
7	Read the [PX2 specification](../../../resources/spec/PIXL-2.md) and [registry](../../../runtime/pixl/registry-v2.json), including their family extension. Discover the installed runner's help or MCP schemas before using the operations below. Existing PX1 and older PX2 projects retain their declared semantics; do not manufacture a migration by relabeling their headers.
8	
9	Gather the brief and sources, target use, actual sample bytes and verdicts, confirmed style choices, applicable adoption decisions and proofs, member inventory, destination choices, and authorized provider scope. Read `workflow STATE --root ROOT`, `family STATE [OUTPUT] --root ROOT`, and `jobs STATE --root ROOT` before extending or retrying existing work. `family` verifies retained files and reports current selection, requirements, pending jobs and historical snapshot drift. It changes no state.
10	
11	Open the exact nominated sample X and its retained observations. Confirm its sample task is done and that its passing verdicts answer the family-relevant question. A replaced or rejected candidate cannot serve as the approved baseline merely because its old PNG remains. A sample that demonstrated a front idle pose does not establish all-direction walk contacts or diagonal tile seams; use the [sample operation](intake-sample.md) to exercise that uncertainty before scaling it.
12	
13	## Save the members and collective requirements first
14	
15	Use the normal decode/edit/encode/validate/expected-hash commit sequence. Record only fields defined in the current specification. Before files exist, save F plans rather than invented X identities.
16	
17	1. Each production F names the exact sample candidate through `bs`. Its producer T lists that X in `ip` and the sample T directly in `dp`. Retain the applicable contract, confirmed choices, adoption D and executed proof; the baseline link does not replace those requirements.
18	2. Make a delivery T and a report-kind F. Set this F's `bs` to the same sample, `mb` to the distinct ordered member F IDs, and `ds` to the same project's destination I choices. The sample output itself may be a member. Other members must be production outputs with the same baseline. List every producer as a direct prerequisite of the delivery T and the baseline X as its input. A family cannot contain itself or another family delivery.
19	3. Define member Q criteria and separate collective Q criteria before results. The family needs a continuity criterion with an observable condition and appropriate evidence mode. State the actual comparison: for example, consistent equipment placement across the requested directions, grounded feet across the cycle, or matching shared boundaries across the required tile transitions. Add engine criteria when required by this destination; a target name alone does not create an engine verdict.
20	4. Save destination choices with their sources, owner and rationale: target project and version, intended paths/names, slicing or tile mapping, pivots, timing, sampling, scale, alpha or atlas rules as applicable. Missing choices remain unresolved; observed/proposed values remain distinct from confirmation. Such choices block delivery activation/completion, while useful member files can still be retained.
21	
22	Commit this plan before collecting verdicts. Keep the project's actual dimensions, style and acceptance conditions; example values are not defaults. `ready` and `workflow` apply activation blockers. Retaining a package has narrower prerequisites and does not grant production adoption or delivery acceptance.
23	
24	## Produce members, compare them, and preserve rejection
25	
26	Run the [provider recovery operation](provider-recovery.md) for each required real generation attempt. It saves the exact request before dispatch and imports actual downloaded bytes as an unaccepted candidate. Read the family report as well as jobs: a member or baseline attempt may be outside the delivery task's forward context packet. For `prepared`, `unknown`, `submitted` or `running` work, resolve the reported action before another attempt or snapshot. An unknown attempt requires the saved request/history and actual provider reconciliation; missing service access leaves that attempt unknown. Do not invent a job ID or infer that a request was never received.
27	
28	Evaluate each member against its own requirements and approved baseline. Keep mechanical measurements, visual observations, temporal or neighborhood comparisons, and engine results separate. A contact sheet is useful comparison evidence, but the actual task determines the required additional inspection:
29	
30	| Family | Inspection to perform and retain |
31	| --- | --- |
32	| Static sprites or variants | Compare actual members and baseline at native scale and enlarged scale; inspect silhouette, volume, equipment landmarks, palette/ramp use, lighting and edge treatment against this project's contract. |
33	| Animation or directions | Play the actual sequence at its intended timing, including loop boundaries and required direction changes. Inspect contact poses and individual frames for anchor drift, sliding, volume changes and direction mapping. Save which files/frames, playback timing, context and observed defect or pass condition support the verdict. |
34	| Tiles or transitions | Assemble repeated neighborhoods using the actual members, including the edges, corners, diagonals and material transitions this game requires. Inspect seams, repeat visibility and projection in those arrangements. Retain the arrangement/mapping and images or observations identifying the compared files. |
35	
36	A dimension or palette check cannot supply these visual judgments. If playback, neighborhood assembly or visual access is unavailable, retain that precise boundary and leave its criterion unavailable/unperformed. Do not write a passing visual receipt for an unseen artifact. When an inspection fails, retain X/E/V and its actual defect, create a revised X at a new path, inspect the revision, and nominate it only with its own current evidence. A successful generation request does not answer the member's acceptance criteria.
37	
38	## Retain and review the exact delivery
39	
40	When the baseline is still eligible and every planned member has a nominee on a done task, inspect the family report for pending jobs and blockers. The delivery task must be open or active for retention. Invoke:
41	
42	```text
43	family-snapshot STORE OUTPUT CANDIDATE --expect HASH --root ROOT
44	family STATE OUTPUT --root ROOT
45	```
46	
47	MCP equivalents are `pixl_family_snapshot` with `store`, `output_id`, `candidate_id`, `expect`, and `pixl_family` with `path` and optional `output`. The server supplies the project root. Reload and reconcile after a stale-hash error; do not overwrite state or repeat remote generation.
48	
49	Snapshot retains actual member copies and a canonical manifest under the store's content-addressed `deliveries/` directory, then publishes a new manifest X with its exact constituent references. Its `accepted: false` means retention created no nomination, verdict or task completion. `remote_executed: false` describes this local operation. Read the resulting manifest and report, verify member order and copied-file identities, and use the copied files for collective review and destination testing. A successful copy does not demonstrate continuity.
50	
51	Nominate the intended manifest candidate through the normal saved-state operation. Evaluate each collective Q against this exact manifest, baseline, copied members, destination choices and current plan. Retain actual observation files, then bind E/V to the full candidate/criterion semantic scope. Save a continuity failure independently from per-member passes. Revise the implicated member and repeat its checks, then take a new snapshot; preserve the rejected family candidate and observations.
52	
53	Published manifest candidates and their constituent X identities are immutable. Member selection, baseline, membership or destination changes leave old packages intact. Reopen affected completed work and supersede stale verdicts/receipts, save the changed plan, and evaluate a new snapshot. The report identifies drift; recomputing an old receipt hash cannot make a historical package current.
54	
55	## Destination boundary and cold handoff
56	
57	Use the target engine and the retained files to exercise the applicable import behavior: frame slicing and order, pivots/contact alignment, timing and loop transitions, direction mapping, texture sampling/display scale, alpha/atlas edges, tile neighbor mapping, or required material/lighting behavior. Record the actual engine/project version, files tested, settings and observed outcome. Metadata inspection alone does not establish engine acceptance.
58	
59	If the engine or target project is unavailable, still deliver links to the retained manifest and useful files. Record an unavailable V with `ev=[]` and the precise missing capability; keep delivery unfinished. Leave the concrete next action, such as importing the named copied sheet into the specified target scene, applying the saved slice/pivot/timing settings, and playing the listed loop and direction transitions. State that destination acceptance is unverified. Do not turn missing engine access into a visual rejection or a fabricated live receipt.
60	
61	Commit a handoff containing the state path and observed revision/hash, family output and manifest candidate, package and copied-file locations, baseline and selected member IDs, relevant failed/unavailable verdicts, pending job IDs and last observed states, and the next task with its required context and action. An N record can point to the retained records/tasks; retain the human-readable instructions in project evidence as needed.
62	
63	A cold session starts with `family`, `workflow` and `jobs` against that root, then retrieves focused `context` and opens the cited artifacts and observations. Reconcile unknown jobs first, review reported plan/selection drift before new evaluation, and execute only the outstanding check or revision. Mark the delivery T done only after every declared criterion on its current nominee passes and prerequisites are done. Finish with the useful files, actual verification, unresolved limits and actionable handoff, without claiming art quality or engine readiness from local fixtures.
64

Do not write a passing visual receipt for an unseen artifact. When an inspection fails, retain X/E/V and its actual defect, create a revised X at a new path, inspect the revision, and nominate it only with its own current evidence. A successful generation request does not answer the member's acceptance criteria.

## Retain and review the exact delivery

When the baseline is still eligible and every planned member has a nominee on a done task, inspect the family report for pending jobs and blockers. The delivery task must be open or active for retention. Invoke:

```text
family-snapshot STORE OUTPUT CANDIDATE --expect HASH --root ROOT
family STATE OUTPUT --root ROOT
```

MCP equivalents are `pixl_family_snapshot` with `store`, `output_id`, `candidate_id`, `expect`, and `pixl_family` with `path` and optional `output`. The server supplies the project root. Reload and reconcile after a stale-hash error; do not overwrite state or repeat remote generation.

Snapshot retains actual member copies and a canonical manifest under the store's content-addressed `deliveries/` directory, then publishes a new manifest X with its exact constituent references. Its `accepted: false` means retention created no nomination, verdict or task completion. `remote_executed: false` describes this local operation. Read the resulting manifest and report, verify member order and copied-file identities, and use the copied files for collective review and destination testing. A successful copy does not demonstrate continuity.

Nominate the intended manifest candidate through the normal saved-state operation. Evaluate each collective Q against this exact manifest, baseline, copied members, destination choices and current plan. Retain actual observation files, then bind E/V to the full candidate/criterion semantic scope. Save a continuity failure independently from per-member passes. Revise the implicated member and repeat its checks, then take a new snapshot; preserve the rejected family candidate and observations.

Published manifest candidates and their constituent X identities are immutable. Member selection, baseline, membership or destination changes leave old packages intact. Reopen affected completed work and supersede stale verdicts/receipts, save the changed plan, and evaluate a new snapshot. The report identifies drift; recomputing an old receipt hash cannot make a historical package current.

## Destination boundary and cold handoff

Use the target engine and the retained files to exercise the applicable import behavior: frame slicing and order, pivots/contact alignment, timing and loop transitions, direction mapping, texture sampling/display scale, alpha/atlas edges, tile neighbor mapping, or required material/lighting behavior. Record the actual engine/project version, files tested, settings and observed outcome. Metadata inspection alone does not establish engine acceptance.

If the engine or target project is unavailable, still deliver links to the retained manifest and useful files. Record an unavailable V with `ev=[]` and the precise missing capability; keep delivery unfinished. Leave the concrete next action, such as importing the named copied sheet into the specified target scene, applying the saved slice/pivot/timing settings, and playing the listed loop and direction transitions. State that destination acceptance is unverified. Do not turn missing engine access into a visual rejection or a fabricated live receipt.

Commit a handoff containing the state path and observed revision/hash, family output and manifest candidate, package and copied-file locations, baseline and selected member IDs, relevant failed/unavailable verdicts, pending job IDs and last observed states, and the next task with its required context and action. An N record can point to the retained records/tasks; retain the human-readable instructions in project evidence as needed.

A cold session starts with `family`, `workflow` and `jobs` against that root, then retrieves focused `context` and opens the cited artifacts and observations. Reconcile unknown jobs first, review reported plan/selection drift before new evaluation, and execute only the outstanding check or revision. Mark the delivery T done only after every declared criterion on its current nominee passes and prerequisites are done. Finish with the useful files, actual verification, unresolved limits and actionable handoff, without claiming art quality or engine readiness from local fixtures.

7	
8	## Understand and allocate
9	
10	Read the project's instructions and available source overview/index/MOC, then verify its pointers against the relevant entry points. If no useful overview exists, retain a focused map of the consumers and backend transitions you actually inspect. If it already has `plar.txt`, read the queue and refresh affected rows. Use CodeGraph first when the project has a `.codegraph/` index; otherwise use the host's code tools. Follow actual UI/renderer consumers through imports, manifests, loaders and backend state transitions. Group shared visual roles into one asset with multiple consumers. A function without an image does not automatically need one.
11	
12	Inspect existing art and the visible UI when available. Distinguish missing files, placeholders, reusable assets, visual mismatches and intentionally procedural/text-only elements. Note dynamic paths or unavailable modules in coverage.unresolved. Scope claims to the code and runtime actually inspected; a filename search is not exhaustive coverage.
13	
14	For each visual role, connect:
15	- Purpose and visible states to file/symbol/usage locations.
16	- Applicable canvas/frame geometry, projection, reference style, edge/alpha policy, timing, pivots, tile rules and import behavior to their sources.
17	- The output destination, checks at the actual display size, dependencies, unresolved choices and one concrete next action.
18	
19	Preserve explicit requirements, observations, proposals and unknowns separately. Use only relevant properties; do not invent a palette, alpha ban or resolution to fill a template. Record user instructions in a small project brief file when they are not already addressable. References convey style; measurements of them do not automatically become rejection rules. When visual input is required, add source-bound references with an explicit role (style, identity, pose, layout, palette, mask or motion) and instructions stating what to preserve.
20	
21	## Save and use
22	
23	Read [the format and operations](references/format.md) when creating or editing the work list. `pixl_plar_save` validates the supplied document, binds new local sources and retains previous versions using an expected hash. `pixl_plar_read` returns queue summaries; pass `asset_id` for the complete selected row and its source/dependency context. Focused reads also return transitive dependency requirements/issues, actual source hashes, absolute project paths, visual references and a derived production view with pending jobs and acceptance state. Use that view to choose resumption versus new preparation; an editable status label is not production evidence. Pass the requirements_hash to a delegate; it changes with relevant requirements or source bytes, not unrelated queue progress. The portable CLI provides the same operations. Ordinary file editing is also supported; re-read and validate afterward.
24	
25	For refresh, read the queue before editing. Its changes report identifies drift and transitive dependents; after a save, or with `plar read --since PRIOR_HASH`, it compares authored requirements against retained history. Treat file-level impact as a prompt to inspect affected consumers, not proof every asset needs regeneration. Check the source overview and changed entry points for newly introduced consumers that no prior row could mention. Preserve unchanged requirements and existing IDs; distinguish a moved destination from a new visual role.
26	
27	A useful row can remain actionable with open questions. Resolve consequential unknowns for the selected action from the project, references or user; continue independent assets. Preserve stable IDs on refresh, retain superseded work as deferred with a reason, and inspect changed sources before deliberately updating their hashes. Update the queue after production and integration, linking retained evidence rather than copying provider job history.
28	
29	## Hand off to production
30	
31	For an asset request, continue through [PIXL](../pixl/SKILL.md) once the selected row is understood. A complete existing brief can go directly to production without a repository-wide scan. Give a delegated specialist the absolute project root, this skill/PIXL locations, PLAR path and asset ID, current user constraints and authorization, available references, and expected files/checks. Do not assume the child has the parent's conversation. Use the [shared delegation contract](../pixl/references/delegation.md) for caller questions and results.
32	
33	PIXL uses the authenticated **official PixelLab API**, through its exposed MCP tools or the supported HTTP adapter, for paid generation within the user's authorized work. Discover the actual operation schema and carry the selected requirements into its arguments. Existing authorization persists; ask only for a missing consequential choice or scope expansion. Development test settings belong to their harness and do not define production policy.
34	
35	For the first concrete candidate, use [selected-asset preparation](references/prepare.md): one local operation translates the reviewed contract into the existing PX2 plan and prepares its first durable request. Continue normal dispatch, retrieval and review through the host's actual PixelLab connection. Single-output preparation links its retained work into PLAR; inspect the allocation result and repair any concurrent-update conflict without duplicating the job. Reviewed changed requirements use the same operation's explicit revision path after pending work is resolved. `pixl_commit` accepts inline JSON, so a host need not encode and write a temporary wire file. Keep provider execution, returned bytes, visual judgment and engine integration distinct. Return actual delivered paths, review findings, integration status and the updated next action. An `integrated` label in PLAR is a caller claim, not runtime certification.

requirements.name: transparent-background

requirements.name: check-mark-asymmetrical-arms

requirements.name: geometry
requirements.check: Decoded image is exactly 16x16 pixels with a single static frame (no horizontal strip, no extra canvas).

requirements.name: transparent-background
requirements.check: The background is transparent: pixels outside the subject have alpha 0 and no opaque matte, box or fringe fills the cell. Partial alpha on subject pixels is permitted; binary alpha is not required.

requirements.name: check-mark-asymmetrical-arms
requirements.check: The image visibly uses a check mark with asymmetrical arms: the mark is not mirror-symmetric about its vertex. Asymmetry may come, for example, from clearly unequal arm lengths or from clearly different arm angles/directions; unequal length is one example, not the required condition. The mark conveys successful completion. Either arm may be the longer one, and stroke weight, colour treatment and construction are not restricted by this criterion.

requirements.name: ready-meaning
requirements.check: Viewed alone, the image reads as successful completion (Ready) rather than activity, failure, pause, or the idle Start control.

requirements.name: readability-1x-3x
requirements.check: Composited on #172336, the silhouette is readable at 1x and at 3x nearest-neighbor scale, with no essential detail (including the asymmetry of the check-mark arms) lost into the panel colour.

requirements.name: cool-blue-accent
requirements.check: The dominant colour treatment visibly relates to the existing UI's cool blue accent as seen in assets/start.svg (#70b9ed). This is a visual relationship judgement, not an exact-hex or palette-count rule.

requirements.name: silhouette-without-color
requirements.check: In a grayscale/desaturated view at 1x and 3x, the Ready mark still has a distinct identifiable shape (its meaning is carried by form, not only hue).

requirements.name: sample-pixel-craft
requirements.check: As a representative family sample, the image shows deliberate pixel-art construction: clean pixel clusters and edges, no noisy stray pixels, blur or downscaled-illustration artifacts, and a treatment that could plausibly be extended to Working, Retry and Paused.

1	# Candidate inspection artifact and operation contract, version 1
2	
3	This operation operates on saved PX2 candidates using existing X/E/V records. It
4	adds no UDL syntax. The runtime prepares exact local inputs and verifies retained
5	records; callers supply actual observations and criterion judgments. Preparation,
6	measurement, declared review, host viewing evidence and engine execution are distinct.
7	
8	## Image delivery through MCP
9	
10	The read-only `pixl_inspection` accepts optional `view_ids` (1–8 distinct IDs,
11	requiring `packet_id`). After validating the retained packet it captures and
12	rechecks each selected PNG against the saved hash and dimensions. It returns
13	unmodified MCP image blocks and `image_payloads` metadata: view ID, zero-based
14	index among image blocks, SHA-256 and `payload_size` [width,height]. The combined
15	encoded files are limited to 8 MiB; request fewer views when exceeded. Unknown
16	views or changed bytes fail rather than returning partial/unverified images.
17	Omitting selection retains the existing text/report operation. This adds no
18	saved-state or manifest fields and creates no observations/verdicts. Encoded
19	payload dimensions do not certify physical display size, downstream host
20	resizing, actual viewing or artistic acceptance.
21	
22	## API and publication
23	
24	`prepare(folder, expected, candidate_id, packet_id, options, root=None)` requires a
25	saved raster X with a matching F owner and C, saved owner task and required Q.
26	`folder` must be a project subdirectory; root defaults to its parent. `expected`
27	is the current canonical state hash. IDs must be valid PIXL identifiers, fresh,
28	and leave enough of the 96-character limit for generated suffixes.
29	
30	Options are closed: required `references` (distinct local S/X IDs; `[]` is explicit),
31	`scale` (integer 2..16), `backgrounds` (nonempty distinct `#RRGGBB` or `checkerboard`);
32	optional `max_side` (64..2048, default 1024), `contexts` (default []). Contexts require
33	explicit `source_frame`. Options impose no universal artistic rules.
34	
35	Each context is one of these closed objects, with a distinct nonempty name and a
36	source ID in the candidate plus explicit references:
37	
38	```json
39	{"name":"walk","kind":"frames","source":"candidate","source_frame":0,

78	{"tool":"pixl_inspection_prepare","arguments":{"store":".pixl","expect":"HASH","candidate_id":"candidate","packet_id":"packet","options":{"references":[],"scale":8,"backgrounds":["#ffffff"]}}}

87	Every encoded input, decoded frame, native transparent view, native background view,

101	
102	`rendering` has exactly `inputs`, `views`, `measurements`, `options`,
103	`context_observations`. Inputs have `source`, `path`, `sha256`, `id`. Views add `id`
104	to the renderer's `path`, `source`, `frame`, `context`, `scale`, `background`, `crop`,
105	`width`, `height`, `sha256`. Paths inside the manifest are relative to its directory.
106	IDs are `PACKET.input.N` and `PACKET.view.N`, zero-based in deterministic render order.
107	Files live at `STORE/inspections/MANIFEST_SHA256/`; the report is `manifest.json`.
108	Views returned to a host have project-relative paths, ready for a root-confined viewer.
109	
110	Packet X metadata is closed and typed: `inspection=packet` (Symbol), `version=1`,
111	`candidate` (Ref), `scope` (ordered original semantic Refs), `files` (ordered retained
112	input then view Refs). Auxiliary X metadata is `inspection=file` (Symbol), `source`
113	(Ref). The loader checks original bodies/hashes, ownership, semantic scope, typed

# Candidate inspection artifact and operation contract, version 1

This operation operates on saved PX2 candidates using existing X/E/V records. It
adds no UDL syntax. The runtime prepares exact local inputs and verifies retained
records; callers supply actual observations and criterion judgments. Preparation,
measurement, declared review, host viewing evidence and engine execution are distinct.

## Image delivery through MCP

The read-only `pixl_inspection` accepts optional `view_ids` (1–8 distinct IDs,
requiring `packet_id`). After validating the retained packet it captures and
rechecks each selected PNG against the saved hash and dimensions. It returns
unmodified MCP image blocks and `image_payloads` metadata: view ID, zero-based
index among image blocks, SHA-256 and `payload_size` [width,height]. The combined
encoded files are limited to 8 MiB; request fewer views when exceeded. Unknown
views or changed bytes fail rather than returning partial/unverified images.
Omitting selection retains the existing text/report operation. This adds no
saved-state or manifest fields and creates no observations/verdicts. Encoded
payload dimensions do not certify physical display size, downstream host
resizing, actual viewing or artistic acceptance.

## API and publication

`prepare(folder, expected, candidate_id, packet_id, options, root=None)` requires a
saved raster X with a matching F owner and C, saved owner task and required Q.
`folder` must be a project subdirectory; root defaults to its parent. `expected`
is the current canonical state hash. IDs must be valid PIXL identifiers, fresh,
and leave enough of the 96-character limit for generated suffixes.

Options are closed: required `references` (distinct local S/X IDs; `[]` is explicit),
`scale` (integer 2..16), `backgrounds` (nonempty distinct `#RRGGBB` or `checkerboard`);
optional `max_side` (64..2048, default 1024), `contexts` (default []). Contexts require
explicit `source_frame`. Options impose no universal artistic rules.

Each context is one of these closed objects, with a distinct nonempty name and a
source ID in the candidate plus explicit references:

```json
{"name":"walk","kind":"frames","source":"candidate","source_frame":0,
 "rects":[[0,0,16,16],[16,0,16,16]],"durations_ms":[100,null],
 "pivots":[[8,15],null]}
```

`source_frame` selects an existing zero-based decoded source frame, even for static
images. Rectangles are ordered `[x,y,width,height]`, with nonnegative integer origins,
positive dimensions and complete containment in that frame. `durations_ms` and
`pivots` have exactly the same length as `rects`; duration entries are positive
integer milliseconds or null, pivots are local in-bounds integer `[x,y]` or null.
Unknown values remain null. Individual frames and a comparison strip are retained.
The strip uses common-pivot alignment only if every pivot is known; otherwise it
uses top-left sequential placement. Timing observations do not create animation.

```json
{"name":"neighborhood","kind":"tiles","source":"candidate","source_frame":0,
 "tile_size":[16,16],"grid":[[0,1],[2,3]]}
```

Tile dimensions are positive integers and must divide the selected source exactly.
The nonempty rectangular grid is an array of top-to-bottom rows, with left-to-right
entries; each integer is a zero-based row-major source tile index. The declared
neighborhood is retained with exact RGBA placement. Every horizontal and vertical
neighbor pair reports differing adjacent RGBA edge-pixel counts, never an automatic
seam verdict. Boolean and fractional values are not valid integer fields.

Public adapters use the same request semantics:

```text
inspection-prepare STORE CANDIDATE PACKET OPTIONS_JSON --expect HASH --root ROOT
inspection-review STORE PACKET REVIEW_ID REVIEW_JSON --expect HASH --root ROOT
inspection STATE [PACKET] --root ROOT
```

CLI JSON arguments are local JSON file paths. MCP root is the configured project
root, and the closed tool envelopes are:

```json
{"tool":"pixl_inspection","arguments":{"path":".pixl/state.px","packet_id":"packet"}}
{"tool":"pixl_inspection_prepare","arguments":{"store":".pixl","expect":"HASH","candidate_id":"candidate","packet_id":"packet","options":{"references":[],"scale":8,"backgrounds":["#ffffff"]}}}
{"tool":"pixl_inspection_review","arguments":{"store":".pixl","expect":"HASH","packet_id":"packet","review_id":"review","observation":{}}}
```

`packet_id` is optional only for `pixl_inspection`; the other shown argument keys
are required. The review's observation placeholder must be replaced by the complete
closed review object described below.

Source bytes are captured once and checked against their saved hashes before rendering.
Every encoded input, decoded frame, native transparent view, native background view,
integer-nearest enlarged background view and requested context is retained. Large views
use complete logical crops before enlargement. Packet preparation creates auxiliary
X records of kind `reference` for inputs/views and a kind `report` X for its JSON.
It changes no nomination, task status, E or V. Publication uses ordinary store CAS;
failed publication may leave unreferenced immutable files, as with existing delivery.

The closed manifest keys are `version` (integer 1), `kind` (`packet`), `packet`,
`candidate`, `output`, `task`, `created_at` (timezone-aware timestamp),
`source_state_sha256`, `records`, `rendering`. Each original semantic record has
exactly `id`, `kind`, `fields` (lossless codec tagged JSON), `sha256` (record hash).
The original semantic proof scope includes the candidate, output, contract, required
criteria, explicit references and their semantic dependencies. Mutable task/project
workflow records are excluded by `graph.proof_scope`; task identity is retained.

`rendering` has exactly `inputs`, `views`, `measurements`, `options`,
`context_observations`. Inputs have `source`, `path`, `sha256`, `id`. Views add `id`
to the renderer's `path`, `source`, `frame`, `context`, `scale`, `background`, `crop`,
`width`, `height`, `sha256`. Paths inside the manifest are relative to its directory.
IDs are `PACKET.input.N` and `PACKET.view.N`, zero-based in deterministic render order.
Files live at `STORE/inspections/MANIFEST_SHA256/`; the report is `manifest.json`.
Views returned to a host have project-relative paths, ready for a root-confined viewer.

Packet X metadata is closed and typed: `inspection=packet` (Symbol), `version=1`,
`candidate` (Ref), `scope` (ordered original semantic Refs), `files` (ordered retained
input then view Refs). Auxiliary X metadata is `inspection=file` (Symbol), `source`
(Ref). The loader checks original bodies/hashes, ownership, semantic scope, typed
projection, canonical manifest bytes and every retained file. It deterministically
re-renders retained inputs to validate all nested rendering metadata and exact bytes.
This intentionally trades read cost for a complete closed rendering check.

Renderer ceilings apply equally to preparation and retained packet verification:
64 MiB/source, 256 MiB aggregate sources, 16,384 decoded pixels/axis, 16,777,216 pixels
per frame, 1,024 frames/source, 67,108,864 aggregate decoded pixels, 65,536 exact visible
colors/frame, 4,096 views, 2,048 delivered pixels/axis, 64 MiB/encoded view,
512 MiB aggregate returned files and 134,217,728 rendered pixels. The 65,537th visible
color rejects instead of truncating. Manifests additionally have the codec's 16 MiB
limit. Context-specific limits remain those documented by the renderer.

Prepare returns store `revision`, `hash`, `state`, plus `packet`, `manifest`, `views`,
`measurements`, `criteria`, `files_verified:true`. Criterion entries have `id`, `name`,
`check`, `domain`, `mode`, `status`, `verdict`. Missing verdicts are `unperformed`.

## Explicit review

`review(folder, expected, packet_id, review_id, observation, root=None)` requires
fresh IDs and current retained bindings. A done task must first be reopened. The
closed observation object requires `reviewer`, `observed_at`, `observations`,
`verdicts`, `next_action`, `limitations`. Reviewer names a saved A; observation time
must have an explicit UTC offset and lie between preparation and local recording.
This is caller-declared time, not an attestation that viewing happened.

Each observation has exactly `view`, `delivered_size`, `note`. View IDs must belong to
this packet and cannot repeat. Dimensions are two positive integers or null. Null
means the host has not established dimensions; never copy file dimensions into an
unknown host delivery. Notes and next action are nonempty text; limitations is a
list of nonempty strings, which may be empty.

Each verdict has exactly `criterion`, `status`, `reason`, `supersedes`. Criteria must
be distinct and required by this packet's original output. Reasons are nonempty.
Local criteria accept pass/fail; engine-domain or live-mode criteria accept only
unavailable, without E. Visual/continuity or visual-mode failures need at least one
observed candidate-source view; viewing only references cannot establish a candidate
failure. Visual/continuity or visual-mode passes require every prepared view, including reference and
context native/enlarged variants, observed at its prepared dimensions. Unknown or
resized deliveries cannot satisfy complete coverage. This verifies declaration
consistency; actual viewing transcripts remain separate evidence. Mechanical criteria
with local evidence mode do not require image-view coverage. Their verdicts still
require an explicit caller judgment against the saved criterion; measurements are
not automatically promoted to verdicts.

`supersedes` is null if no current V exists; otherwise it must name that exact current
V for this candidate/criterion. The operation marks that V obsolete and retains it.
It creates `REVIEW.verdict.N` for each declaration and `REVIEW.evidence.N` for each
performed criterion. E binds the exact original candidate/Q scope plus packet, review
and all retained files. It uses the criterion's required mode and declared outcome.
The saved-plan ordering and ordinary graph/store gates remain authoritative.
Omitted criteria stay unperformed unless they already have an existing current V.
A separate candidate inherits no V. Task nomination and status are unchanged.

Review JSON has exactly `version:1`, `kind:review`, `packet`, `review`, `recorded_at`,
`source_state_sha256`, `observation`, `coverage`. Its report X metadata is exactly
`inspection=review` (Symbol), `version=1`, `packet` (Ref). Coverage has `complete`,
`observed`, `missing`, `resized`, `unknown_size`; ID lists are sorted. Review returns
store commit fields plus `packet`, `review`, `verdicts` (new IDs), `coverage`,
`files_verified:true`. Retained next actions and limitations remain in observation.

## Cold reporting and history

`report(doc, root, packet_id=None)` returns `hash`, `files_verified:true`, `packets`.
Each packet has identity/ownership/time, views, measurements, context observations,
original criteria text with current candidate verdicts, `binding_drift` (changed
original semantic IDs), retained `reviews`, `files_verified:true`,
`visual_quality_verified:false`, `engine_import_verified:false`. Those final flags
state the runtime's limits; declared caller verdicts are represented separately.

Proper amendments remain readable with original criterion text; new reviews against
stale packets are rejected. Earlier E/V must be superseded under existing rules when
amending their dependencies. Reporting validates even obsolete inspection E against
its original retained closure and validates review V projections. Closed equivalence
preserves exact scalar types: booleans cannot stand in for integers and fractional
JSON representations cannot replace integer rendering metadata. Retained reads enforce
remaining aggregate source-byte limits before reading each input. Relocation is safe
when the project and its relative store layout are copied together.

These guarantees belong to the inspection APIs. Ordinary generic X records remain
mutable under existing semantics; arbitrary generic edits are not inspection
publication. The loader detects inconsistent retained files, bodies and projections;
it does not establish cryptographic authorship or guarantee discovery after arbitrary
coordinated generic rewriting. Historical receipts are never edited to imply new tests.

1	# Reviewed task completion
2	
3	`task-complete STORE TASK CANDIDATE... --expect HASH --root ROOT` and
4	`pixl_task_complete({store,expect,task_id,candidates})` nominate explicit existing
5	candidates and complete their PX2 task. This is a local publication operation;
6	it creates no criteria, decisions, evidence, verdicts, asset files or provider calls.
7	It adds no UDL fields and preserves the existing registry/lifecycle semantics.
8	
9	Every planned output needs exactly one supplied candidate owned by that output.
10	Every saved required criterion must already have a current passing verdict for
11	that candidate. Missing, failed, unavailable or stale acceptance cannot complete.
12	All normal prerequisite, choice, adoption, baseline and file-binding checks apply.
13	Prepared/unknown/submitted/running jobs on this task must be reconciled first.
14	Dropped tasks and changes to already-completed selections require explicit reopening.
15	
16	The expected hash is checked under the store lock. The complete transition sequence
17	is validated before publication. An open or blocked task publishes the ordinary
18	active revision and then the done revision, retaining both snapshots; an active
19	task needs one revision. The operation holds the writer lock throughout. Validation
20	failure leaves state unchanged. Storage interruption between publications can leave
21	a valid active state; read workflow/current hash and resume without repeating any
22	provider request. Hard process termination may leave the existing store lock; follow the normal stale-lock owner check before recovery. This is not a multi-file all-or-nothing transaction.
23	
24	An already-done task with the same selection and expected hash returns
25	`already_complete:true` without another revision. Results include state/hash/revision,
26	selected candidate IDs, task ID, publication history and explicit
27	`acceptance_created:false` / `remote_executed:false`. Files still need the caller's
28	assigned destination integration and actual review; this operation only publishes
29	completion supported by the existing saved acceptance plan.
30	
31	PLAR-bound continuation uses the [allocation/revision contract](asset-preparation.md#allocation-and-revised-work). Pending attempts for the same explicitly tagged asset exclude new jobs even under different task/output IDs. it creates no criteria, decisions, evidence, verdicts, asset files or provider calls.
It adds no UDL fields and preserves the existing registry/lifecycle semantics.

Every saved required criterion must already have a current passing verdict for
that candidate. Missing, failed, unavailable or stale acceptance cannot complete.
All normal prerequisite, choice, adoption, baseline and file-binding checks apply.
Prepared/unknown/submitted/running jobs on this task must be reconciled first.
Dropped tasks and changes to already-completed selections require explicit reopening.

The expected hash is checked under the store lock. The complete transition sequence
